conjecture: Q191 / WZZ 2401.14632 Problem 5.2: find a combinatorial proof of the M-convexity of cylindric skew Schur polynomials based on their tableau interpretation, i.e. one that does NOT consume Lam 2008 Cor 8.5 (the motive stated verbatim in the paragraph above their Problem 5.1) or Lee 2019 Cor 5.

tree.approach: ANSWERED. Work in the periodic Maya-diagram (bead) model. A semistandard cylindric skew tableau is a chain of n-periodic bead configurations; its weight is the increment sequence of the single scalar u^t = sum_{i=1..m} x^t_i. The M-convex exchange axiom is then realised by sliding ONE bead of ONE row of the chain one site to the left. Main theorem is strictly stronger than WZZ Cor 4.9: supp(s^c_{lambda/mu}(x_1..x_l)) = {alpha : sort(alpha) <| lambdahat} = P_lambdahat cap Z^l, with lambdahat computed by an explicit greedy chain.

children.approach: Prop 2.4 CLOSED IN FULL: cylindric shapes <-> C^{n,m} via x_i = R_i + i, where R_i is the right-hand column of row i (rows indexed DOWNWARD, so row lengths INCREASE and the sign is +i, not -i). Containment, box count per fundamental domain, and 'at most one box per column' <-> interlacing are all proved directly from that formula; no window/local-reduction argument is used. TWO errors made and corrected in session: (a) first draft claimed a bijection with periodic bead SETS -- false, a bead set determines the path only up to diagonal translation and the lost datum is Postnikov's shift d; (b) first draft of the sign used R_i - i -- false, it is not even strictly increasing. The sign was fixed by RENDERING WZZ Figure 5.1 and reading the boxes off the picture, not by guessing.

Lemma 3.1: with x^{t-1}=p and x^{t+1}=r held fixed, the admissible middle rows x^t form a BOX prod_i [L_i,U_i], L_i = max(p_i, r_{i-1}+1), U_i = min(p_{i+1}-1, r_i). The two horizontal-strip conditions constrain x^t_i only through p and r, never through x^t_j for j != i; strict increase of x^t is automatic. Verified exhaustively: 380/380 feasible (p,r) instances over 2<=n<=5, 290 middle shapes total.

Lemma 3.2: sum_{i=1..m}(L_i+U_i) = sum_{i=1..m}(p_i+r_i). Proof is max+min=sum plus one wrap-around term, which contributes exactly +n. THE CYLINDRIC CASE WORKS BECAUSE OF THE PERIODICITY, NOT IN SPITE OF IT: drop the wrap-around and one gets sum(p+r)-n and the false conclusion that cylindric Bender-Knuth fails. I made exactly that slip in first derivation; the computation caught it. Verified 470/470 feasible (p,r) pairs over 2<=n<=6.

Cor 3.3: x^t_i -> L_i + U_i - x^t_i is an involution on chains interchanging alpha_t and alpha_{t+1}. Reproves Postnikov's symmetry theorem for cylindric skew Schur functions, so the argument does not have to cite it. Verified on COEFFICIENTS (not merely support) in 339 instances.

Cor 3.4: if alpha_t > alpha_{t+1} then alpha - e_t + e_{t+1} is a weight, realised by sliding ONE bead of row x^t one site left. This is the two-site Maya move the brief asked for. Proof: if x^t were at the left corner of its box then alpha_t = mu_- <= N/2 = alpha_{t+1} by the palindrome identity.

Prop 4.2: P(W_l) is a dominance order ideal. Robin-Hood step (Lemma 4.1, proved from scratch: choose i minimal with nu_i > sigma_i, j minimal > i with nu_j < sigma_j, then slide to the block endpoints a,b so that nu - e_a + e_b is again a partition) plus S_l-stability plus the exchange move. Prop 4.2 (prop:ideal) MINUS its two combinatorial inputs, formalised in Lean 4 / Mathlib v4.30.0 as `RobinHood.dominance_ideal`. Statement: for W : Set (Nat -> Int) stable under transpositions Equiv.swap i j with i,j < l (hperm, standing for cor:bk = sibling node `cylindric-bender-knuth`) and under sliding one unit rightwards across a descent (hexch, standing for cor:exchange = sibling node `exchange-move`), if nu in W is a partition with <= l parts and sigma <| nu is a partition of the same size with <= l parts, then sigma in W. hperm and hexch are HYPOTHESES OF THE THEOREM, not sorries: this node does NOT cover cor:bk or cor:exchange, which remain `proved` on their own sibling nodes. P(W_l) = {nu in W | IsPart l nu} because W is S_l-stable, so no sorting function is constructed.
TWO DELIVERABLES BEYOND THE PAPER. (1) The paper says 'by induction on the (finite) number of steps' and never names the terminating measure; Lean will not accept that. The measure is `RobinHood.gap l sigma nu = sum_{r<l} (psum nu r - psum sigma r)`, the area between the two partial-sum profiles: >= 0 iff sigma <| nu (`gap_nonneg`), and a Robin Hood step drops it strictly because the profile falls by one on the window (a,b] and r=b is in range (`gap_lt`). The induction is on (gap l sigma nu).toNat. This confirms the measure conjectured in the 2026-09-22 c2 LEAN brief. (2) The side condition b < l is NOT a conclusion of `robin_hood_step` and had to be recovered from the size equation psum (ex a b nu) l = psum nu l (`exch_snd_lt`): a < l because nu a >= nu b + 2 >= 2 > 0, and then the size equation forces b < l. The paper never states this and the gap measure is undefined without it.
SHARPENING: the size and non-negativity conditions on W itself (every beta in W has sum beta = d and beta >= 0), which the brief listed as hypothesis (hsum), are NOT consumed -- the needed instances are carried by IsPart and by the theorem's own psum sigma l = psum nu l. They are therefore not assumed.
SORTING BRIDGE: the paper's appeal to S_l-stability plus sorting collapses to a single pointwise identity, `ex a (a+1) (nu o swap (a+1) b) = (ex a b nu) o swap (a+1) b` -- the near exchange on the twisted vector IS the far exchange, twisted; swap is an involution, so one more hperm untwists it.
CONTROLS. `hyps_satisfiable`: W = univ satisfies hperm and hexch, so the hypotheses are not contradictory (weak -- the conclusion is free). `hexch_load_bearing`: the S_2-orbit W_0 = {(3,1),(1,3)} satisfies EVERY hypothesis except hexch, with nu = (3,1) in W_0, sigma = (2,2) a partition of 4 with sigma <| nu, and sigma NOT in W_0. So the theorem genuinely consumes cor:exchange; it is not an order-theoretic fact about S_l-stable sets.

Lemma 5.2 / Prop 5.4: the greedy chain g^t_i = min(g^{t-1}_{i+1} - 1, lambda_i) dominates every chain COORDINATEWISE in every row, hence maximises u^r for all r SIMULTANEOUSLY; since alpha_1+...+alpha_r = u^r - u^0 telescopes, sort(gamma) is the unique dominance maximum of P(W_l). Verified 462/462.  [2026-09-21 c2] GAP (iii) OF THE PAPER CLOSED AND CORRECTED.  The recursion g^t_i = min(g^{t-1}_{i+1}-1, lambda_i) contains no ell, so lambda-hat does not depend on the alphabet AT ALL: T_ell is empty below ellmin (where the polynomial is 0 and lambda-hat undefined) and lambda-hat is CONSTANT at and above ellmin, with exactly ellmin parts.  The paper's gap (iii) said lambda-hat 'grows with ell until ell reaches the minimal chain length' -- there is no growth regime and that sentence is withdrawn.  Written out in full as Lemma 4.1 of proofs/2026-09-21-c2-affine-stanley-321-avoiding.tex; verified 4568 instances, 0 failures.

Prop 6.2: {alpha in N^l : sort(alpha) <| lambdahat} is M-convex, proved from scratch by the tight-set argument (tight sets of a submodular rho are closed under union/intersection; if no exchange worked, the union S* of witnesses would satisfy beta(S*) > alpha(S*) = rho(S*)). Included so that the proof cites nothing -- in particular NOT Rado's theorem.

The BROWSE addendum to the brief proposed Q198 (the converse of Naprienko 2301.12110 Lemma 4.4) as the opening move, on the reading that a ribbon's one-bead hop k -> K+1 is the shape of an M-convexity exchange. It is not the move this problem needs. A RIBBON of size r is one bead hopping r sites, jumping freely over occupied sites; a HORIZONTAL STRIP of size r is several beads hopping right with pairwise DISJOINT closed trajectories (Lemma 2.6). Cylindric skew Schur functions are built from horizontal strips, so the ribbon move is the wrong local move. The move that actually implements the exchange axiom is smaller: one bead in one row of the chain slides ONE site.
children.reason: Category error in the brief, not in Naprienko: Lemma 4.4 is about ribbons (rim hooks), and cylindric skew Schur tableaux are chains of horizontal strips. Ribbon bead-hops and horizontal-strip bead-hops are different moves -- the first jumps over beads, the second may not. Q198 remains a well-posed question about ribbons; it is simply not on the path to Q191.
